descriptionChirho: A Christological title for Jesus Christ used almost exclusively in Revelation, designating him as the sacrificial and exalted Lamb of God who was slain and now reigns. Multilingual evidence uniformly capitalizes: spa 'Cordero,' hin 'मेम्ना/मेम्ने,' arb 'الحَمَلِ,' kor '어린양의,' swa 'Mwanakondoo.' All 29 occurrences across nominative, genitive, and dative singular forms carry this titular, theological sense.

A literal young sheep or lamb, used in Jesus' pastoral command to Peter in John 21:15 ('Feed my lambs'). Distinguished from the Christological title by lowercase usage and plural form referring to actual sheep or metaphorical flock members. Multilingual evidence: spa 'corderitos,' hin 'मेमनों-को,' arb 'حُمْلانِي,' kor '어린양들을,' swa 'wana-kondoo.' The diminutive or plural form reinforces the literal, non-titular meaning.
